messages:
noah: Heads-up — nightly mini-kbench (small-batch, kv-prefill config) flagged a consistent ~18-22% latency regression on H100 for seqlen=1024 when prefill=true vs previous baseline. Run: https://ci.internal/runs/78923 :eyes:

noah: Minimal repro snippet from the harness:
```
kbench --arch h100 --seq-len 1024 --batch 2 --prefill true --profile micro --iter 500
# observed p95 78ms (baseline 64ms)
```

vikram: ugh. did the autotune picks change? any kernel switch in the candidate list?

noah: Looks like the kernel selector favoured the new quantized-kv path (kv-opt-v2) for ampere/h100 when batch<=4. Autotune CI promoted it yesterday after the nightly sweep.

maria: Can you paste the kernel pick logs from the run? I want to check the decision traces (seqlen partitioning + heuristic score).

noah: pasted snippet from runtime log:
```
[kernel-selector] seqlen=1024 batch=2 arch=h100 -> picked kv-opt-v2 score=0.82 (prefill_gain=0.15, batch_penalty=0.02, memory_headroom=0.05)
[autotune] candidate-set size=5 -> promoted kv-opt-v2 at 2027-06-12T02:10:12Z
```

olivia: Interesting — kv-opt-v2 reduces memory footprint but has a more expensive per-token kernel in small batches. We probably tuned it for throughput at batch>=8.

vikram: That matches. Our heuristic currently biases toward memory_headroom for private deployments; for small-batch interactive workloads that's hurting latency.

maria: For triage: can we run a quick microprobe comparing kv-opt-v1 vs kv-opt-v2 across batch=1..8 and seqlen=256/512/1024 on H100? Add perf counters (sm_eff, l2_bw) + p95/p99.

noah: scheduled a probe matrix on perf-lab (job id 79011). quick results attached in gist: https://gist.internal/79011

perf-bot: Probe job 79011 completed: summary: kv-opt-v2 shows +20% p95 at batch<=2 for seqlen>=512, but wins by ~12% at batch>=8. See /artifacts/79011/summary.json

olivia: Can we tweak the selector rules to include an explicit small-batch latency penalty weight? e.g., add fe.weight_small_batch_latency = 0.25 for interactive routes.

vikram: Agreed. Also want to add a runtime override: route.config.experimental.prefer_low_latency = true to short-circuit selection for API routes tagged interactive.

maria: Meanwhile, rolling back promotion sounds safest until we publish a targeted heuristic adjust. Can we revert candidate promotion for h100 small-batch profiles only?

noah: I opened a rollback PR on the autotune registry: https://scm.internal/r/autotune/rollbacks/1213 — it sets policy: do-not-promote for kv-opt-v2 when batch_max<=4.

maria: Perfect. Also adding a nightly microbench check to the perf CI that fails if p95 increases >10% over baseline for any seqlen at batch<=4.

vikram: Good. Add the failing run to the perf alert channel and tag infra: @olivia @noah.

noah: Will do. Also adding a quick reproducer command for local devs:
```
# reproduce locally (docker perf image)
docker run --rm -it redwood/perf:latest bash -lc "kbench --arch h100 --seq-len 1024 --batch 2 --prefill true --iter 200 --profile micro"
```

olivia: FYI I dug into kernel-level counters: the v2 path triggers additional cross-SM syncs with small batches; L2 efficiency drops by ~9%. That explains higher latency despite lower memory usage.

maria: Ok action list:
- roll back kv-opt-v2 promotion for batch<=4 (noah)
- add small-batch p95 gate to nightly perf CI (maria)
- add selector override flag for interactive routes (vikram)
- run extended microprobe for seqlen 256/512/1024 batch 1..8 (olivia)

noah: assigned and started rollback; I'll post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Rollback PR merged by noah at 2027-06-12T09:42:10Z — autotune registry rebuilt.

olivia: running extended microprobe now, should have results in ~45m.

noah: thanks all. once we have probe numbers we can tune the selector weights and re-promote with a canary targeting batch>=8 only. :partyparrot:
